correctness.rationale: Individually rational coalitions cannot repeat a role because one -n overwhelms at most n-2 positive edges; hence they are cliques, of size <=3. Positive welfare forbids singletons. If T triples and P pairs, n=3T+2P and q=T+P>=a, so T<=n-2a. Nash product equals 2^(3T). The proposed counts T=b+c-a, AB=a-c, AC=a-b are nonnegative and cover all a,b,c agents, achieving the bound. Equality forces exactly a coalitions, all containing one A-agent; labeling yields the factorial ratio. Direct independent literal payoff enumeration of all partitions for 116 ordered class-size triples of n<=7 matched both optimum and optimizer count.

evidence: Pagano–Schlenga Section 3 proves the clique/IR reduction and discusses tripartite graphs in a PartitionIntoTriangles hardness reduction (even in its Appendix), but does not supply the all-(a,b,c) closed maximum and optimizer count for complete tripartite graphs. Bullinger–Chatziafratis–Shahkar evaluate utilitarian welfare, which permits singletons and does not imply Nash-positive optima. Known maximum-matchings tables count different combinatorial objects.

value.rationale: The majority threshold and exact count of optimal labeled coalition partitions are meaningful closed invariants of the canonical complete-multipartite hedonic benchmark; the optimum and optimizer degeneracy distinguish welfare objectives despite shared graph structure.

final_claim: For complete tripartite mutual friendship K_(a,b,c), a>=b>=c>=0, n>=2, cross-class valuation +1, same-class -n, max Nash geometric welfare among individually rational partitions is zero if a>b+c; otherwise it is 2^(3(b+c-a)/n). In the positive case every optimizer has b+c-a triples, a-c pairs of types AB, a-b of types AC, and the exact labeled optimizer count is a!b!c!/[(b+c-a)!(a-c)!(a-b)!].
